text:
maria: Quick sync — we're handing off the continuous-batcher heuristic tuning work to ops for the next sprint. Want to make sure dashboards and runbook are in a good state before shift change.
kevin: Thanks — what specifically should ops verify? metrics + alerts?
anika: Priority: batch_utilization (p50/p90), queue_depth (p50/p95), tokens_per_sec (per gpu), kvcache_hitrate, kernel_choice_switches. Also a new metric: microbatch_coalescence_rate.
sam: Added a checklist in the ticket but TL;DR: dashboards, alert thresholds, sampling for traces, and spike playbook.
maria: Ops action items I care about: 1) confirm Grafana panels exist and show latest queries, 2) add alert for sustained drop in kvcache_hitrate > 15% for 2m, 3) alert for queue_depth_p95 > 750 for 1m (we saw tail slowdowns), 4) make a runbook snippet for kernel fallback events.
kevin: Example queries I used for the panels:
```
# batch utilization
sum(rate(batch_formed_tokens_total[1m])) / sum(rate/batcher_capacity_tokens[1m])) * 100

# kvcache hit rate
sum(kvcache_hits{model=~".*"}) / sum(kvcache_lookups{model=~".*"})
```
anika: For traces, please sample 1% of requests where batch_size > 1 and token_count > 256 so we can inspect kernel selection outcomes.
sam: Ops-bot note: will attach the current Grafana links and the alert rules we inherit from staging. @ops-bot can you paste links?
ops-bot: Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/ci-batching/continuous-batcher-overview
ops-bot: Dashboard panels: batch_utilization (panel id 12), queue_depth (panel id 17), token_rate (panel id 23), kvcache_hitrate (panel id 31), kernel_switches (panel id 42)
kevin: One more: add a short table panel showing top N kernels by p99 latency over last 30m so oncall can see if kernel selection regressed.
maria: Also capture a small perf-regression play: if kernel_switches increase > 3x coincident with p99 latency > 200ms and batch_utilization drops > 20%, trigger a SEV-2 path and notify #eng-runtime-pager.
anika: I've uploaded a profiling snippet to the ticket — includes raw nvprof traces and a small python script that converts to flamegraphs. Ops: please ensure access to S3 path /perf/profiles/cont-batcher/2412345678/ is available to oncall.
sam: Will validate S3 ACLs and add a short retrieval snippet to runbook:
```
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-perf/profiles/cont-batcher/2412345678/trace.tar.gz ./ && tar -xzvf trace.tar.gz
```
maria: For the telemetry team: consider adding a derived metric `token_efficiency = tokens_served / gpu_seconds` so we can monitor cost-efficiency alongside throughput. Put it on a weekly rollup too.
kevin: Ops, if you need quick synthetic loads to validate dashboards, use this curl sequence that simulates mixed token lengths and forces batching:
```
for i in $(seq 1 50); do
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/generate -d '{"prompt":"lorem ipsum","max_tokens":512}' &
done
```
ops-bot: Acknowledged. I'll create the alert PR and add the runbook entry. Tagging @kevin @maria for review when done. :thumbsup: 
maria: Thanks — once alerts are live let's have a quick 15-min handoff demo tomorrow 10:15am PT to walk through the panels and the playbook flow.
anika: I'll join and bring a short slide showing the kernel-selection cases we observed (quantized vs fp16).
sam: Perfect. I'll also add a pointer to the continuous-batcher canary job so ops can run it on demand.
kevin: One last nit: please set the dashboard time window default to 30m and ensure timezone is UTC so we avoid confusion during oncall.
maria: Agreed. That should be everything for the handoff. Thanks team!
